admin.webPushDescription: Tells members on their devices when Ruchoir is closed. Each person turns it on for their browser. The signal goes through the browser vendor's notification service (Google, Apple, Mozilla, Microsoft) with no content at all: no author, no conversation, no text. Turned off, existing subscriptions are forgotten.

import.exportSlackStep1: In the Slack admin: Settings → Import/Export Data → Export, then download and unpack the ZIP. A standard export holds public channels only.
import.exportSlackStep2: On the Ruchoir host: convert-slack.py --export <unpacked dir> --out <archive>. Attachments are downloaded from Slack during the conversion, so convert while the export is fresh: its links expire with it.
import.exportTeamsStep1: In Entra ID, register an application with the read-only application permissions that convert-teams.py --help-app lists, grant admin consent, and put its secret in a file only you can read.
import.exportTeamsStep2: On the Ruchoir host: convert-teams.py --tenant <tenant> --client-id <application> --secret-file <file> --out <archive>. Each team's channels and file library are read; chats (private conversations) stay in Teams.
import.exportSeal: Seal the archive with a passphrase (symmetric gpg): it is the one you will be asked for here.
import.exportMattermostStep1: On the Mattermost server: mmctl export create, then retrieve the ZIP it produces.
import.exportMattermostStep2: On the Ruchoir host: convert-mattermost.py --export <unpacked dir> --out <archive>. Private channels and direct messages are included.
import.exportNextcloudStep1: Copy packages/importer/export-nextcloud.sh onto the Nextcloud server.
import.exportNextcloudStep2: Run it against the instance's config: export-nextcloud.sh --config <path>/config.php --out /tmp/export. It reads the database and files, never writing anything back to Nextcloud.
import.exportNextcloudStep3: It seals the archive and prints a passphrase: note it down, it is kept nowhere.
